answer: Leaves are added one at a time: each is countersigned by two walnut that have never signed and are spent by signing, so no cohort fans out in parallel. The k-th leaf bonds k opal to the reef, whose tip advances only when the bond lands. A second tree is barred because a walnut must already stand on the reef's tip to sign for a newcomer. One operator's thousandth identity bonds a thousand opal; a thousand identities lock 500,500 opal.
